newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian kidnap rate eases but still alarming.
newsitem.headline: Colombian kidnap rate eases but still alarming.

text.p: The number of kidnappings in Colombia has dropped by nearly one-third so far this year, but it remains a world leader in terms of the total number of abductions, authorities said on Thursday.
Alberto Villamizar, head of President Ernesto Samper's anti-kidnapping office, said 197 kidnappings occurred across the country between January and March, down from 290 in the same period last year.
"The drop is due to closer coordination among security forces responsible for fighting this crime," Villamizar told Reuters.

He stressed the overall number of kidnappings was still extremely high, however, and said "we can't let our guard down" because Colombia is plagued with the highest incidence of the crime anywhere in the world.

Of the 197 cases from January to March, Villamizar said 54 victims had been rescued and 50 others were freed, most in exchange for ransom money. Eighty-five others were still held hostage and eight were known to have been killed, he said.
Official police statistics show a total of 328 kidnappings in Colombia during the first quarter of the year, a drop of just 10 percent from the same period in 1996.

Villamizar said the discrepancy with his own figures was due to shoddy reporting by police statisticians and the fact that the same kidnap case is often reported to more than one branch of the National Police.
